prompt:
You are a careful equity research analyst. Assess the competitive advantages (economic moat) and pricing power of the publicly listed company "Robinhood Markets, Inc." (ticker HOOD), and list its competitors. Use the most recent information you know. Never invent figures: use null when unsure. Be specific (products, numbers, years).

Reply with ONLY one JSON object, no other text, in exactly this shape:
{
 "name": "official company name", "ticker": "HOOD", "industry": "industry in a few words",
 "markets": ["the main product markets it competes in"],
 "mission": {"statement": "the company's own official mission statement, word for word as it publishes it; null if you are not sure of the exact wording (never paraphrase here)",
             "source": "where it is published, e.g. company website or 2025 annual report, or null",
             "plain": "what the mission means, in one short simple sentence"},
 "about": {"plain": "3-4 short sentences explaining what the company does, in simple everyday words a 12-year-old would understand; no jargon",
           "customers": "who buys from it, in one simple sentence",
           "everyday": "one sentence linking it to something ordinary people know or use, or null",
           "money": [ {"part": "business line in simple words", "share": decimal share of sales or null, "plain": "what it sells there, in a few simple words", "tag": "main|new|moonshot"} ]  (its main ways of making money, largest first, up to 6; also include any new business line or one with explosive, moonshot potential even if its sales are still small. tag: "main" = an established line that brings in a large part of sales; "new" = launched or entered in roughly the last 3 years; "moonshot" = could grow many times over or reshape the company, e.g. a new technology or market, even if unproven. Give each line one tag, the one that fits best)},
 "summary": "2-3 plain-English sentences on whether and why it has a competitive advantage",
 "pricingPower": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "specific evidence, e.g. price rises and what happened to volumes"},
 "moats": [ {"source": one of ["Brand and intangible assets","Switching costs","Network effects","Cost advantage and scale","Efficient scale","Counter-positioning","Process power (hard-to-copy know-how)","Cornered resource (exclusive asset or talent)"], "strength": "strong|moderate|weak|none", "evidence": "one or two specific sentences"} ]  (all 8 sources, in that order),
 "customers": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "customer satisfaction and loyalty: retention, NPS, reviews, repeat purchase"},
 "talent": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "ability to attract and keep top talent: employer rankings, reputation, pay"},
 "product": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "is the product best in class? independent benchmarks, awards, ecosystem"},
 "competitors": [ {"name": "company name", "ticker": "main listing ticker (exchange suffix if not US, e.g. 005930.KS) or null if private",
                   "usTicker": "ticker of its US listing or ADR that files reports with the SEC, or null", "overlap": "high|medium|low",
                   "note": "where they compete"} ]  (every significant competitor, most direct first, up to 15; include major private ones with ticker null),
 "estimates": [ {"name": "company name", "fy": "FY2025", "currency": "USD", "revenueUSDm": number, "revenueGrowth3y": decimal, "grossMargin": decimal, "operatingMargin": decimal, "netMargin": decimal} ]
   (approximate latest fiscal-year figures for the company itself and for every listed competitor; decimals, e.g. 0.42; null if unknown),
 "marketShare": [ {"market": "market name", "measure": "revenue|units|shipments|...", "latestYear": "2025", "earlierYear": "2020",
                   "rows": [ {"name": "company name", "latest": decimal or null, "earlier": decimal or null} ] } ]  (up to 3 of its main markets, the company and its main rivals),
 "threats": ["specific things that could weaken its advantage"],
 "ceo": {"name": "current CEO", "founder": true or false, "since": "YYYY", "background": "e.g. electrical engineer, Stanford MBA"},
 "checklist": { "<id>": {"verdict": "yes|partly|no|unknown", "evidence": "one specific sentence with names, numbers or examples"} }  for EVERY id below:
   "c1": Rule Breaker #1: is it the leader of an important industry that is still emerging and growing fast?
   "c2": Rule Breaker #2: why do customers choose it over rivals (brand, better value, innovation, culture, leadership), and is that advantage hard to copy and likely to last many years?
   "c3": Rule Breaker #5: do ordinary people recognise the name, is it the default leader in its field (like Google, Amazon, NVIDIA, Tesla, Intuitive Surgical, Netflix), and would customers recommend its product?
   "c4": Does it have an inspiring mission it keeps emphasising, with management driven by purpose rather than money? If it spends 10 years doing this, would it matter?
   "c6": What is the general public consensus about the company and its products or services? When people hear the name, what are the first few descriptive words that come to mind? Start the evidence with those words in quotes (e.g. “innovative, premium, reliable”), then say whether that impression is mostly positive.
   "c7": Is its total addressable market large and growing, riding a secular trend (like CRWD, NVDA, TSLA, AMZN)?
   "c8": Does it have room to expand into big new markets: in its name, its technology or its vision?
   "m1": Is the CEO a visionary with a clear picture of the future?
   "m2": Is the CEO a founder (or acting like one): long-term thinking, working extraordinarily hard, pouring heart and soul into building something that outlives them?
   "m4": Does the CEO lead by serving employees and customers?
   "m5": Has the CEO deliberately built a strong, distinctive culture that keeps inventing new products and technologies?
   "m6": Is the CEO deeply hands-on with the product and technology, ideally with an engineering background?
   "m7": Is the CEO a person of great character who cares about something bigger than profit? For successor CEOs: is stewardship aimed at the benefit of humanity?
   "m7b": Has the CEO been invited to give a commencement speech at a top university (Stanford, Harvard, MIT, etc.)? Name it.
   "m8b": Does the CEO have a distinctive, memorable personality (like Elon Musk, Alex Karp, Larry Page)?
   "m9": Has the CEO a strong record of execution and results?
   "m10": Is the CEO and company known for frugality (like Bezos's door desk)?
   "c10": Do its products solve problems for people all over the world, greatly improving the lives of a very large number of people (like NFLX, GOOG, ISRG)?
   "p2": Is what it builds extremely hard to do, and important to the world?
   "f1": Has revenue grown in almost every one of the last five years?
   "f2": Have gross and operating margins risen over the last five years?
   "f3": Is debt low compared with cash and cash flow, with positive shareholders' equity?
   "f4": Have operating income and operating cash flow risen over the last five years?
   "v1": Is its main product clearly the best in its field, with a practical reason an ordinary person can understand for choosing it over every alternative (like NVIDIA over AMD)?
   "v2": Is it widely seen as one of the best companies to work for (culture, mission, reputation, employer rankings)? Cite rankings.
   "c5": Do its products make the world better? If it disappeared overnight, who would notice and miss it, and why?
 "asOf": "YYYY-MM of the newest information you used"
}

result.name: Robinhood Markets, Inc.
result.industry: Online retail brokerage, crypto trading and consumer fintech
markets: Commission-free US retail stock and options trading
Retail cryptocurrency trading and institutional crypto exchange (Bitstamp)
Prediction markets / event contracts (Rothera exchange joint venture with Susquehanna)
Margin lending, securities lending and cash sweep
Subscription (Robinhood Gold), retirement accounts, managed portfolios (Strategies) and advisor custody (TradePMR)
Consumer banking and credit cards (Robinhood Banking, Gold Card)
International brokerage and crypto (UK, EU stock tokens, Singapore, Canada via WonderFi, Indonesia)

mission.statement: Our mission is to democratize finance for all.
mission.plain: Robinhood wants anyone, not just the rich, to be able to invest and use financial tools cheaply and easily.

about.plain: Robinhood is a phone app that lets people buy and sell shares, options and crypto without paying a fee per trade. It makes money when customers trade, from interest on money customers borrow or leave in their accounts, and from a monthly Gold membership. It also offers retirement accounts, a credit card, banking and bets on real-world events like elections and sports. Most of its customers are younger people in the United States.
about.customers: Mostly younger US retail investors and traders, plus a growing number of wealthier savers, overseas customers and crypto institutions.
about.everyday: Robinhood is the app with the green feather that made free stock trading normal; it had 28.4 million funded customers at the end of June 2026.

money.plain: interest on margin loans, customer cash, lent-out shares and corporate cash
payments from market makers when customers trade options
fees and spreads when customers buy and sell crypto
payments from market makers when customers trade shares
fees on event contracts about sports, politics and the economy
monthly membership with higher interest, bigger IRA match and research
bank accounts for Gold members and tokenized stocks on its own blockchain

result.summary: Robinhood has built a real but still developing advantage: a well-known brand among younger investors, a very low-cost, fast-moving technology platform and a habit of launching new products (prediction markets, banking, tokenized stocks) faster than incumbents. It earned a 47% pre-tax margin on $4,473M of revenue in 2025 while charging $0 commissions, but customers can move to other low-cost brokers easily and much of its revenue depends on volatile retail trading activity, especially crypto and options.

pricingPower.evidence: Robinhood competes on $0 commissions and low fees, so it cannot easily raise headline trading prices; its pricing levers are the $5-a-month Gold subscription (4.8 million subscribers at June 2026, up 39% a year) and spreads on crypto and event contracts, and crypto revenue fell 38% year on year in Q2 2026 to $100M when retail crypto activity cooled.

moats.evidence: Robinhood is the best-known trading app among younger US investors and has 28.4 million funded customers (June 2026), but the brand is also tied to the 2021 GameStop trading restrictions and record regulatory fines, so it is less trusted than Schwab or Fidelity.

Moving a brokerage account via ACATS is free and quick, though Robinhood is raising stickiness with retirement accounts ($26.5B AUC at end-2025), Gold perks, banking deposits (over $3B by June 2026) and its credit card.
One customer's account gains little from others using Robinhood; the main exception is liquidity in its own prediction-market exchange (Rothera) and Bitstamp, where more traders mean tighter markets.

With about 2,900 employees at end-2025 serving 27 million funded customers, Robinhood earned a 47.1% pre-tax margin in 2025 ($2,108M on $4,473M revenue), and $324B of platform assets lets it spread technology costs widely, though Schwab and Fidelity are far larger.
Retail brokerage and crypto trading are crowded with many profitable competitors (Schwab, Fidelity, Interactive Brokers, Webull, Coinbase, Kalshi), so there is no natural limit on entrants.

Robinhood's mobile-first, $0-commission, crypto- and event-contract-friendly model was hard for incumbents to copy without cutting their own revenue; they matched $0 commissions in 2019, but most still avoid prediction markets and tokenized stocks.

Robinhood ships products unusually fast (short selling, banking, Robinhood Chain mainnet, Rothera exchange, Cortex AI assistant in 2025-2026) and now has 13 business lines each above $100M of annualized revenue, a product engine incumbents have struggled to match.
It owns licences (broker-dealer, Bitstamp crypto licences, a CFTC-licensed exchange through Rothera, Singapore CMS licence) but these can be obtained by rivals and give no exclusive asset.

customers.evidence: Funded customers grew 7% to 28.4 million and Gold subscribers 39% to 4.8 million in the year to June 2026, with net deposits of $21.7B in Q2 2026 (28% annualized), showing customers bring more money; NerdWallet rates Robinhood 4.5/5 (best for basic stock trading) but below Fidelity, Interactive Brokers and Schwab, noting it doesn't 'love the gambling features'.

talent.evidence: Robinhood attracts strong engineers with Silicon Valley pay and equity, but its Glassdoor page shows 3.4 out of 5 with 47% recommending it to a friend, and it went through large layoffs in 2022; it is not on major best-employer lists.

product.evidence: Its app is widely seen as the simplest and best-designed for trading and leads in new products (event contracts, tokenized stocks, 24-hour trading), but independent reviews such as NerdWallet rate Fidelity, Interactive Brokers and Schwab higher overall for research, service and breadth.

threats: Dependence on volatile retail trading: crypto revenue fell 38% year on year in Q2 2026 and transaction revenue swings with markets
Payment for order flow, which funds $0 options and stock trading, could be restricted by US regulators
State gaming regulators and lawsuits (e.g. Massachusetts) challenging sports event contracts, now a fast-growing revenue line ($156M in Q2 2026)
Falling interest rates would cut net interest revenue (34% of 2025 revenue)
Low switching costs and fierce competition from Schwab, Fidelity, Interactive Brokers, Webull, Coinbase, Kalshi and Polymarket
Reputation and regulatory risk from past episodes (2021 GameStop restrictions, FINRA fines including $29.75M in March 2025) and from 'gamification' criticism
Execution risk in expanding into banking, international markets and tokenization

ceo.name: Vlad Tenev
ceo.background: Co-founder; Stanford mathematics graduate who left a UCLA mathematics PhD to co-found Robinhood in 2013; co-CEO with Baiju Bhatt until becoming sole CEO in November 2020

c1.evidence: Robinhood leads the mobile-first retail trading and fast-emerging retail prediction-market segments (over 12 billion event contracts traded in 2025), but overall retail brokerage is a mature industry led by Schwab and Fidelity.

c2.evidence: Customers choose it for a simple, well-designed app, $0 commissions, 24-hour and crypto trading and new products like event contracts and a 3% IRA match for Gold members, but rivals can copy most features and switching is easy.

c3.evidence: Robinhood is a household name among younger investors and joined the S&P 500 in September 2025, but it is not the default leader of brokerage and NerdWallet rates it 4.5/5, below Fidelity, Interactive Brokers and Schwab.

c4.evidence: Its mission 'to democratize finance for all' is constantly repeated and drove $0 commissions and fractional shares, though critics say gamified trading and sports event contracts sit uneasily with it.

c6.evidence: “free trading, young investors, meme stocks, risky” – the public sees Robinhood as easy and innovative but also tied to GameStop, gambling-like trading and crypto speculation, so the impression is mixed.

c7.evidence: It rides the secular shift of wealth to younger, mobile-first investors (a multi-trillion-dollar intergenerational transfer), plus crypto, tokenization and prediction markets, and platform assets rose 68% to $324B in 2025.

c8.evidence: It is expanding into banking (over $3B deposits by June 2026), retirement, advisor custody (TradePMR), international markets (over 1 million international funded customers), institutional crypto (Bitstamp) and its own blockchain (Robinhood Chain).

m1.evidence: Vlad Tenev lays out a clear vision of a global financial 'super app' built on tokenized assets and AI (Cortex), and has pushed tokenized stocks and Robinhood Chain ahead of incumbents.

m2.evidence: Tenev co-founded Robinhood in 2013 and has led it since, keeping control through Class B super-voting shares and repeatedly investing for the long term in new products.

m4.evidence: Robinhood's model was built around lower costs for customers, but episodes such as the January 2021 GameStop trading restrictions and the FINRA fines show customer service has not always come first.

m5.evidence: Tenev has built a fast product-shipping culture that now has 13 business lines each above $100M of annualized revenue, launching banking, prediction markets, short selling and a blockchain within about two years.

m6.evidence: Tenev is a Stanford-trained mathematician who started as an engineer and is closely involved in product launches and the technology roadmap, including tokenization and AI.

m7.evidence: Tenev speaks about widening access to finance, but Robinhood's reliance on options, crypto and sports event contracts draws criticism that it profits from risky retail behaviour.

m7b.evidence: Tenev gave the 2019 keynote at UCLA's mathematics department commencement, not a main university-wide ceremony at Stanford, Harvard or MIT.

m8b.evidence: Tenev is a recognisable public figure (notably from his February 2021 congressional testimony on GameStop), but he is not as distinctive a personality as Musk or Karp.

m9.evidence: Under Tenev, revenue rose from $1,358M in 2022 to $4,473M in 2025 and Robinhood swung from a $541M loss in 2023 to $1,883M of net income in 2025.

m10.evidence: Robinhood cut about 23% of staff in 2022 and runs with roughly 2,900 employees, keeping 2026 adjusted costs growing much slower than revenue, but it is not known for Bezos-style frugality.

c10.evidence: It made investing free and accessible for tens of millions of people, mostly in the US, but its impact is narrower than products like Google or Netflix.

p2.evidence: Running a regulated, high-volume brokerage, crypto exchange, bank and prediction-market exchange is hard, but similar services are offered by many established firms.

f1.evidence: Revenue grew from $958M (2020) to $4,473M (2025) but fell 25% in 2022 to $1,358M after the 2021 trading boom.

f2.evidence: Robinhood moved from large losses in 2021-2023 (pre-tax loss of $533M in 2023) to a 36% pre-tax margin in 2024 and 47.1% in 2025.

f3.evidence: At June 2026 corporate cash was about $5.4B against about $2.2B of debt (including a June 2026 convertible notes offering), and stockholders' equity was $9,151M at end-2025.

f4.evidence: Pre-tax income rose from a $533M loss in 2023 to $2,108M in 2025, but operating cash flow was volatile ($1,181M in 2023, -$157M in 2024, $1,638M in 2025).

v1.evidence: It is arguably the easiest, best-designed trading app with unique features (event contracts, tokenized stocks), but Fidelity, Schwab and Interactive Brokers rank higher on overall quality.

v2.evidence: Robinhood is not on major best-employer lists and its Glassdoor rating is about 3.4/5 with 47% recommending it to a friend.

c5.evidence: Millions of young investors would miss its free, simple app and its push made $0 commissions standard across the industry in 2019, though critics argue its trading and betting features also cause harm.
